subject: Fleet slotting & tradeoffs: H100 / A100 / L4 — recommended slotting + fallback playbook

Subject: Fleet slotting & tradeoffs: H100 / A100 / L4 — recommended slotting + fallback playbook

Hi Amira / Triton team,

Quick note to share our preliminary SKU slotting guidance for the Dedicated commitment discussion later today. We ran a short profile of the demo workload you shared and pulled together an initial tradeoff matrix attached (triton-sku-matrix.xlsx). This email summarizes the recommended slotting and operational fallbacks so your procurement and engineering teams have visibility.

Summary / recommendation (short):
- Primary pools: split by workload profile instead of model name.
  - Memory-bound long-context inference (batch/kv-heavy): H100 pool (80GB) — keep here for large LLM checkpoints and 2–8k+ context runs.
  - General-purpose multi-turn chat and fine-tuned generation: A100 40GB pool — best balance of price/perf for sustained throughput and medium contexts.
  - Low-latency, short-context routing and cheaper stateless embeddings: L4 pool — low cost per token for small models and rapid responses.
- Initial fleet mix for the committed Dedicated capacity: start conservative with 35% H100 / 50% A100 / 15% L4 by slot count, with a 25% burst buffer (autoscale) to cover peak-day traffic.
- Fallbacks: route to A100-compatible quantized variants or L4 when H100 slots saturated; degrade to short-context models first for non-critical routes (search, suggestions).

Key rationale: H100 gives headroom for 80GB+ checkpoints and highest batch efficiency for heavy KV-cache reuse — important for your long medical-context flows. A100 (40GB) delivers better cost efficiency at medium sequence lengths because of stronger batching density per dollar. L4 is the cost-optimized fast-path for short queries (embedding, classification) and as a graceful lapse option for non-SLA paths.

Action items we suggest to finalize sizing:
1) 72-hour pilot using 2 production-like routes (one long-context, one chat) so we can collect P95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost/token across pools.
2) Confirm your peak concurrency windows and acceptable P95 targets per route (you previously noted 150ms P95 for UI search).
3) Sign-off on an initial commitment delta (3 months) so we can reserve the slot mix and configure headroom.

Attachments: triton-sku-matrix.xlsx (detailed numbers), latency-p95-compare.png (pilot snapshot).

I'll be on the call at 2pm PT to walk through this.

Thanks,
Priyom

Subject: Re: Fleet slotting & tradeoffs: H100 / A100 / L4 — recommended slotting + fallback playbook

Thanks Priyom — good writeup. A couple of implementation notes from runtime/ops perspective:

- Memory realities: H100 (80GB) is the only practical option for the 1-shot 20k token runs we profiled. A100 40GB can handle ~8–12k realistically when we enable prefix KV caching and streaming, but you need to enforce a 4–8 token overlap guard to avoid OOMs.
- Quantization: for A100 we recommend q4_0/q4_k_mixed profiles for generative workloads to improve packing without notable quality regressions in our evals. L4 we treat as 8-bit quantized by default; good for embeddings and short completion paths.
- Batching and slot sizing: A100 gives denser batching at moderate latencies; H100 shines when you can sustain large batch sizes and reuse KV caches across requests. For Triton, we saw 2.4x throughput improvement on H100 vs A100 on long-context batched runs (pilot traces attached).
- Autoscale buffer: 25% headroom is our conservative baseline; if Triton wants a higher SLA (99.95% p95), push to 40% buffer or reserve extra pre-warmed slots for peak windows.

Operational fallbacks (how to route):
1) If H100 utilization > 85% and queueing spikes, route new long-context requests to A100-quantized variant with a warning header (degraded quality).
2) For non-blocking background workloads (embeddings reindex, batch scoring) shift to L4 when A100+H100 > 90% utilized.
3) For critical, user-facing short chats (UI), prefer A100 over L4 to preserve conversational coherence; only use L4 for caching-based responses or automated suggestions.

I'll prepare a short test plan for the 72-hour run (scripts + perf counters) and upload to the Drive link.

Adding some commercial sizing context so Procurement can see impact to monthly commit pricing and breakpoints:

- Cost assumptions (ballpark): H100 slot ~ $X, A100 slot ~ $Y, L4 slot ~ $Z (we'll attach final committed pricing in the term sheet).
- Effective tokens/slot-hour: for your Triton LLM mix we saw roughly: H100 2.2M tokens/hr (long-context, batched), A100 1.1M tokens/hr (mixed chat), L4 0.9M tokens/hr (short queries, high QPS). These are empirical from our pilot traces — numbers in the spreadsheet.
- Economic mapping: the slot mix (35/50/15) yields per-token costs ~12% lower than a pure H100 deployment for your expected traffic mix while keeping 95th latency targets for long-context paths. Swap costs if you need more low-latency headroom or stronger p95 — shifting 10% from A100 to H100 reduces p95 for long flows but increases cost by ~9%.

Recommended next commercial steps:
1) Procurement to review the term sheet we will send with two commit options: (a) 12-month blended commit with 25% burst allowance, (b) 3-month pilot commit (smaller discount, faster cancellation).
2) If Triton prefers predictability over lowest cost, go with option (a) and commit an additional 10% H100 buffer.

Amira — any preference from your side on commit horizon? If you want, we can model alternate mixes (H100-heavy vs A100-heavy) against your three-month forecast and show cost + latency curves.

—Jordan
